items.title: Gerald Wilson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Komasi was a student at UCLA, and I heard him play, I got him right away. I took him to New York with me when I was with Stix.

ctx.x: Rodney Whitaker, really good, yeah. Well he gets the band, he gets the band together for me there, you know, so they played. Man, they played so good. And I narrated. As we’d be playing, I’d tell the people, like I’d tell them, “okay now, I’m going to talk to you about it here, but here you got to read my lips.” You understand? Like when the president said read my lips? And then I do it, I just – I went – I won the prize. They had a – someone else could have won this prize I won in Detroit this year. There’s a…

because he can move. I don’t know any saxophone player who can move like him today. You know, I mean fast, fast. So anyway, that takes care of that. Oh, and Aram, that’s another – I dedicated that to Aram Khachaturian years ago, years ago I dedicated it to him. And I studied his music, man yeah.
